s1.syndrome_frame: a clinical presentation of respiratory symptoms with a mass in the lung and an expansile lesion in the hyoid bone
salient_findings: a 3.1 × 2.7 × 3.6 cm mass in the right lower lobe
an intensely FDG-avid, partially calcified 4.1 × 2.3 × 2.8 cm expansile lesion within the right hyoid bone
key_facts: 27-year-old man with a history of melanoma
melanoma was 5 mm‐thick and located on the posterior neck
melanoma was treated six years earlier by wide local excision
no sentinel lymph node biopsy or adjuvant therapy was performed
vital signs were within normal limits
physical examination was notable only for scattered breath sounds without stridor
laboratory studies, including complete blood count and metabolic panel, were unremarkable
endobronchial ultrasound–guided fine-needle aspiration of the lung lesion demonstrated a malignant small round blue cell tumor
molecular studies were negative for an EWSR1 translocation
PET/CT showed an FDG-avid right lower lobe mass and an intensely FDG-avid, partially calcified lesion within the right hyoid bone
ultrasound–guided core needle biopsy of the hyoid lesion was nondiagnostic
mid-treatment PET/CT demonstrated a substantial decrease in size and complete metabolic response of the lung mass
development of right neck adenopathy and interval growth of the hyoid bone lesion

shortlist.label: Chordoma
shortlist.why_kept: expansile lesion in the hyoid bone, a rare site for chordoma

raw.rationale: The patient has a history of melanoma, and the development of new lesions, including one in the lung and another in the hyoid bone, suggests metastatic disease. The fact that the lung mass responded to chemotherapy but the hyoid bone lesion did not, and instead grew, could indicate that the hyoid lesion is a metastasis from the original melanoma, which can be more aggressive and less responsive to chemotherapy.

rejected.label: Ewing sarcoma
rejected.why: Molecular studies were negative for an EWSR1 translocation, which is a characteristic genetic abnormality found in Ewing sarcoma.

rejected.label: Primitive neuroectodermal tumor
rejected.why: Similar to Ewing sarcoma, the lack of EWSR1 translocation makes this diagnosis less likely.

rejected.label: Plasmacytoma
rejected.why: The patient's presentation and the nature of the lesions do not strongly suggest a plasma cell disorder.

rejected.label: Chondrosarcoma
rejected.why: The description of the lesions, particularly the lung mass, does not align well with the typical presentation of chondrosarcoma.

rejected.label: Osteosarcoma
rejected.why: The patient's age and the nature of the lesions are not typical for osteosarcoma, which usually presents as a bone tumor in younger individuals or in older adults with specific risk factors.

rejected.label: Lymphoma
rejected.why: While lymphoma can present with widespread disease, the specific characteristics of the lesions in this case, including the presence of a malignant small round blue cell tumor in the lung, do not strongly support lymphoma.

rejected.label: Chordoma
rejected.why: Chordomas are rare tumors that typically arise in the spine or base of the skull, and the patient's presentation does not align well with this diagnosis.
